controls.title: Ensure Safe Links for Office Applications is Enabled
controls.description: Safe Links must rewrite and time-of-click verify URLs inside Office applications, Teams and email.
controls.rationale: Attackers weaponise links after delivery. Time-of-click protection is the only control that catches that.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Users may see warnings or be blocked from opening a rewritten link.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented
controls.auditProcedure: Get-SafeLinksPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableSafeLinksForEmail, EnableSafeLinksForTeams, EnableSafeLinksForOffice, TrackClicks, AllowClickThrough

audit.name: Read the Safe Links policy
audit.payload: Get-SafeLinksPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableSafeLinksForEmail, EnableSafeLinksForTeams, EnableSafeLinksForOffice, TrackClicks, AllowClickThrough | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 -Compress

assertions.failure: Safe Links for Office applications is {actual}; CIS 2.1.1 requires it to be True.
assertions.hint: Set EnableSafeLinksForOffice to $true on the Safe Links policy.

assertions.failure: Safe Links for email is {actual}; links in inbound mail are not being rewritten.
Safe Links for Teams is {actual}; links shared in chat and channels are not scanned at click time.
AllowClickThrough is {actual}, so users can dismiss the warning page and open a blocked URL.
assertions.hint: Set AllowClickThrough to $false so the block page cannot be bypassed.

remediation.name: Enable Safe Links across Office, email and Teams
remediation.payload:
Set-SafeLinksPolicy -Identity 'Standard Preset Security Policy' -EnableSafeLinksForEmail $true -EnableSafeLinksForTeams $true -EnableSafeLinksForOffice $true -TrackClicks $true -AllowClickThrough $false
Get-SafeLinksPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableSafeLinksForEmail, EnableSafeLinksForTeams, EnableSafeLinksForOffice, TrackClicks, AllowClickThrough | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous Safe Links configuration
rollback.payload:
Set-SafeLinksPolicy -Identity 'Standard Preset Security Policy' -EnableSafeLinksForEmail {{EnableSafeLinksForEmail}} -EnableSafeLinksForTeams {{EnableSafeLinksForTeams}} -EnableSafeLinksForOffice {{EnableSafeLinksForOffice}} -TrackClicks {{TrackClicks}} -AllowClickThrough {{AllowClickThrough}}
Get-SafeLinksPolicy | Select-Object Name, EnableSafeLinksForEmail, EnableSafeLinksForTeams, EnableSafeLinksForOffice, TrackClicks, AllowClickThrough | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure the Common Attachment Types Filter is enabled
controls.description: The anti-malware policy must block the common executable attachment types.
controls.rationale: Blocking risky file types at the transport layer removes an entire class of delivery technique.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Common risky attachment types will be blocked.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented

audit.name: Read the common attachment filter
audit.payload: Get-MalwareFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, EnableFileFilter, ZapEnabled | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 -Compress

assertions.failure: The common attachment types filter is {actual}; executable attachments are not being blocked.

remediation.name: Enable the common attachment types filter
remediation.payload:
Set-MalwareFilterPolicy -Identity Default -EnableFileFilter $true
Get-MalwareFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, EnableFileFilter, ZapEnabled | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous attachment filter setting
rollback.payload:
Set-MalwareFilterPolicy -Identity Default -EnableFileFilter {{EnableFileFilter}}
Get-MalwareFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, EnableFileFilter, ZapEnabled | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure Safe Attachments policy is enabled
controls.description: Attachments must be detonated in a sandbox before delivery.
controls.rationale: Signature-based scanning misses novel payloads; detonation catches them before the user does.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Mail delivery may be delayed by up to a few minutes while attachments are scanned.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented

audit.name: Read the Safe Attachments policy
audit.payload: Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy | Select-Object Identity, Enable, Action | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 -Compress

assertions.failure: Safe Attachments is {actual}; attachments are delivered without sandbox detonation.
assertions.hint: Enable the Safe Attachments policy and set its action to Block.

assertions.failure: The Safe Attachments action is {actual}; CIS requires {expected}.
assertions.hint: Set the Safe Attachments action to Block.

remediation.name: Enable Safe Attachments with the Block action
remediation.payload:
Set-SafeAttachmentPolicy -Identity 'Standard Preset Security Policy' -Enable $true -Action Block
Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy | Select-Object Identity, Enable, Action | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous Safe Attachments configuration
rollback.payload:
Set-SafeAttachmentPolicy -Identity 'Standard Preset Security Policy' -Enable {{Enable}} -Action {{Action}}
Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy | Select-Object Identity, Enable, Action | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure that an anti-phishing policy has been created
controls.description: A custom anti-phishing policy with mailbox intelligence and impersonation protection must exist.
controls.rationale: The default policy does not enable impersonation protection, which is what catches business email compromise.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Users may see safety tips and first-contact banners on inbound mail.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented
controls.auditProcedure: Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled, EnableMailboxIntelligence, EnableSpoofIntelligence, PhishThresholdLevel

audit.name: Read the anti-phishing policy
audit.payload: Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled, EnableMailboxIntelligence, EnableSpoofIntelligence, PhishThresholdLevel | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 -Compress

assertions.failure: Mailbox intelligence is {actual}; impersonation of known senders will not be detected.
The phishing threshold is {actual}; CIS requires at least {expected} (Aggressive).

remediation.name: Harden the anti-phishing policy
remediation.payload:
Set-AntiPhishPolicy -Identity 'Office365 AntiPhish Default' -Enabled $true -EnableMailboxIntelligence $true -EnableSpoofIntelligence $true -PhishThresholdLevel 3
Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled, EnableMailboxIntelligence, EnableSpoofIntelligence, PhishThresholdLevel | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous anti-phishing configuration
rollback.payload:
Set-AntiPhishPolicy -Identity 'Office365 AntiPhish Default' -Enabled {{Enabled}} -EnableMailboxIntelligence {{EnableMailboxIntelligence}} -EnableSpoofIntelligence {{EnableSpoofIntelligence}} -PhishThresholdLevel {{PhishThresholdLevel}}
Get-AntiPhishPolicy | Select-Object Name, Enabled, EnableMailboxIntelligence, EnableSpoofIntelligence, PhishThresholdLevel | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure DMARC Records for all Exchange Online domains are published
controls.description: Every accepted domain must publish a DMARC record with a quarantine or reject policy and an aggregate report address.
controls.rationale: Without DMARC, receivers have no instruction on what to do with spoofed mail claiming to be from the organisation.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.auditProcedure:
Resolve-DnsName _dmarc.[domain1.com] txt

Ensure that the record exists and has at minimum the following flags defined as follows:
v=DMARC1; (p=quarantine OR p=reject), pct=100, rua=mailto:<rua-report@example.com>, ruf=mailto:<ruf-report@example.com>

Ensure the Microsoft MOERA domain is also configured.
Resolve-DnsName _dmarc.[tenant].onmicrosoft.com txt
controls.remediationProcedure:
1. For each Exchange Online Accepted Domain, add the following record to DNS:
Record: _dmarc.domain1.com
Type: TXT
Value: v=DMARC1; p=none; pct=100; rua=mailto:<rua-report@example.com>; ruf=mailto:<ruf-report@example.com>
2. This will create a basic DMARC policy that will allow the organization to start monitoring message statistics.
3. One week is enough for data generated by the reports to be useful in understanding email trends and traffic. The final step requires implementing a policy of p=reject OR p=quarantine and pct=100 with the necessary rua and ruf email addresses defined.

audit.name: Resolve the DMARC record for every accepted domain

assertions.failure: These domains do not publish an enforcing DMARC record: {actual}.
assertions.hint: Publish a TXT record at _dmarc.<domain> with v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; pct=100; rua=mailto:dmarc@<domain>.

controls.title: Ensure the connection filter IP allow list is not used
controls.description: The hosted connection filter policy must not carry an IP allow list.
controls.rationale: Allow-listed source IPs bypass spam and phishing filtering entirely; a compromised partner relay becomes a direct path to every inbox.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented

audit.name: Read the connection filter IP allow list
audit.payload: Get-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, IPAllowList, EnableSafeList | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 -Compress

assertions.failure: The connection filter allow-lists {actual}; mail from these addresses skips spam and phishing filtering.
assertions.hint: Clear the IP allow list with Set-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy -Identity Default -IPAllowList @().

remediation.name: Clear the connection filter IP allow list
remediation.payload:
Set-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy -Identity Default -IPAllowList @()
Get-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, IPAllowList, EnableSafeList | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure the connection filter safe list is off
controls.description: The Microsoft-managed safe list on the hosted connection filter policy must be disabled.
controls.rationale: The safe list allows a third-party maintained set of senders to bypass filtering, outside the tenant's control.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Some emails previously trusted may be filtered as spam.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented

audit.name: Read the connection filter safe list flag

assertions.failure: The connection filter safe list is {actual}; a Microsoft-maintained sender list bypasses your filtering.

remediation.name: Turn the connection filter safe list off
remediation.payload:
Set-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy -Identity Default -EnableSafeList $false
Get-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, EnableSafeList | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

rollback.name: Restore the previous safe list setting
rollback.payload:
Set-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy -Identity Default -EnableSafeList {{EnableSafeList}}
Get-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, EnableSafeList | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure inbound anti-spam policies do not contain allowed domains
controls.description: No domain may be allow-listed in the hosted content filter policy.
controls.rationale: An allow-listed domain is trivially spoofable and bypasses all inbound protection for that sender.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Emails from previously allowed domains may be filtered as spam.
controls.cisControl: CIS Control 9: Email and Web Browser Protections
controls.nistCategory: PR.PS-05 Installation of unauthorized software is prevented

assertions.failure: The inbound anti-spam policy allow-lists {actual}; mail claiming to be from those domains bypasses filtering.
assertions.hint: Clear AllowedSenderDomains on every hosted content filter policy.

remediation.name: Remove allowed sender domains
remediation.payload:
Set-HostedContentFilterPolicy -Identity Default -AllowedSenderDomains @()
Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy | Select-Object Identity, AllowedSenderDomains | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

controls.title: Ensure the Account Provisioning Activity report is reviewed weekly
controls.description: An analyst must review account provisioning activity every week.
controls.rationale: Unexpected account creation is one of the earliest signals of a persistent intruder.
controls.nistCategory: DE.CM-09 Computing hardware and software are monitored
controls.auditProcedure:
To audit using the UI:
1. Navigate to Microsoft Purview https://compliance.microsoft.com.
2. Select Audit to open the audit search.
3. Set Activities to 'Added user' and review the results for the past week.
controls.remediationProcedure: Assign the weekly review to a named analyst and record the outcome in the ticketing system. There is no tenant setting to change.

audit.name: Manual review of account provisioning activity
audit.payload:
1. Navigate to Microsoft Purview at https://compliance.microsoft.com.
2. Open Audit and search the 'Added user' activity for the last seven days.
3. Confirm every new account maps to an approved joiner request.
4. Record the review and its outcome against this control.

controls.title: Ensure Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is enabled and configured
controls.description: Defender for Cloud Apps must be connected to the tenant with app discovery and session policies in place.
controls.rationale: Shadow IT and OAuth application abuse are invisible without a CASB.
controls.nistCategory: DE.CM-09 Computing hardware and software are monitored
controls.auditProcedure: Navigate to the Microsoft Defender portal and confirm Cloud Apps > Settings shows an active connection and at least one file policy.
controls.remediationProcedure: Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps. Requires Microsoft 365 E5 or the Defender for Cloud Apps standalone licence.
controls.requiredLicense: Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Cloud Apps standalone

audit.name: Read the Defender for Cloud Apps connection state

assertions.failure: Defender for Cloud Apps is {actual}; shadow IT and OAuth grants are not being monitored.
assertions.hint: Licence and enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, then configure app discovery and a file policy.
